item.title: China rejects EU request for voluntary curbs on hybrid car exports as trade talks begin in Beijing: What it means
item.description: China has rejected the EU’s request for voluntary curbs on hybrid car exports, adding a fresh hurdle to trade talks in Beijing, Financial Times reported. Brussels is considering import caps or tariff-rate quotas as Chinese carmakers expand their share of Europe’s auto market.
item.dc:creator: Bhanu Pratap
item.content:encoded: China has rejected a request from the European Union for voluntary curbs on hybrid car exports to the bloc, adding a new flashpoint to trade talks between Brussels and Beijing as the two sides seek to avoid a wider trade conflict, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday, citing two diplomats briefed on the discussions.Earlier, the European Commission had asked China to voluntarily limit shipments of China-made hybrid vehicles to Europe, according to the report.The development comes as EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič travels to Beijing for two days of talks with Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao.The negotiations aim to address the EU's widening trade deficit with China, with Chinese exports of relatively low-cost electric and hybrid vehicles emerging as a key issue.Why are hybrids becoming EU-China trade flashpoint?The EU has been increasingly concerned about the rapid growth of Chinese vehicle sales in the European market.Chinese carmakers captured a record share of nearly 12% of Europe's new-car market in August and accounted for roughly one in three plug-in hybrid sales in the region, Bloomberg reported.Therefore, the surge has put hybrid vehicles alongside electric cars at the centre of the EU's concerns over China's growing automotive exports.The European Commission is now considering safeguard measures that could restrict imports following a surge in Chinese-made hybrids entering the European market.One option under consideration is a tariff-rate quota, under which imports would be allowed up to a specified volume, while vehicles brought in above that threshold could face additional tariffs, Bloomberg reported.The proposed restrictions would be time-limited, said the Bloomberg report.Why did EU seek voluntary export curbs?The EU's initial approach was to seek a negotiated solution rather than immediately impose new trade restrictions.The European Commission had sought China's agreement to voluntarily limit hybrid exports to Europe.The Financial Times on 17 September 17 reported that Beijing could face higher tariffs if it did not agree to such restrictions.The commission hopes to get Beijing to accept a unilateral EU mechanism to cap hybrid imports, rather than having China voluntarily restrict exports, according to FT.What happens next?The issue is expected to feature prominently in the latest round of EU-China trade talks in Beijing, which are starting on Thursday.Šefčovič and his team are scheduled to hold two days of negotiations with Chinese officials, with discussions aimed at reducing the trade imbalance without triggering a broader confrontation, according to The Guardian.The outcome could influence whether the European Commission proceeds with its proposed safeguard measures.The commission is also reportedly viewing hybrids as a potential test case. If the measures are effective, similar tools could potentially be considered for other sectors where the EU sees significant trade imbalances, according to Bloomberg.For the EU, the continued growth in Chinese vehicle exports is adding pressure to address concerns over an uneven trading relationship.China has a large trade surplus with Europe, and the hybrid-car dispute could therefore risk becoming part of a broader trade dispute.

item.title: Starlink row: Govt rubbishes Elon Musk's remarks on ‘oligarchs’ as ‘baseless’, hails India's ‘fair’ framework
item.description: The Ministry of Communications dismissed SpaceX CEO Elon Musk's claim that the Starlink satellite communication service in India is being “blocked by certain oligarchs.”
item.dc:creator: Akriti Anand
item.content:encoded: The Ministry of Communications issued a statement on Thursday, following SpaceX CEO Elon Musk's remarks against Indian ‘oligarchs’ for blocking Starlink communication services in the country. The government said it has put in place a “fair and non-discriminatory authorisation framework” for all telecommunication services, including satellite communication services."The suggestion that the framework or its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived," the ministry said without explicitly referring to Musk's comments a day earlier.On Wednesday, a social media post by Elon Musk went viral. The SpaceX and Tesla boss had shared ‘DogeDesigner's' post, which gave pointers on why India needs Starlink.Musk reshared the X post, saying, "Unfortunately, we are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people. You can guess who they are. This is a crime against the people of India!"What Indian govt said: ‘Fair and non-discriminatory' frameworkThe Ministry of Communications did not name Musk in its statement on Thursday, but acknowledged the post, which was “being circulated on social media, regarding the fairness of India’s regulatory framework for satellite communication services and suggesting that it is being applied in a discriminatory manner.”Rubbishing Musk's claim, the minister said, “…the suggestion that the framework or its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived.”The ministry said, “The Government has put in place a fair and non-discriminatory authorisation framework for all telecommunication services, including satellite communication services.”“Under this, telecom licences have been granted to three Global Mobile Personal Communication by Satellite services based on non-geosynchronous satellite orbit based satellite communications, as part of its commitment to enable provision of satellite communication services in India,” the government said.Under the terms and conditions of the license, every such licensee is required to demonstrate compliance with security conditions. This is aimed at ensuring that services provided meet various security requirements to ensure safety of all users and their data,” the minister added.The statement noted that the security assessment is currently underway for all three licensees. “As and when this process is completed for a licensed entity, it may proceed to the next step of seeking assignment of spectrum,” the ministry stated.The government further informed that at present, all three entities are broadly at the same regulatory stage. “As such, the suggestion that the framework or its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived,” it said.India's Starlink projectIndia’s two biggest private telecom operators, Reliance Jio Infocomm Ltd. and Bharti Airtel, together account for roughly 910 million broadband subscribers, more than 80 percent of the country’s market, according to the latest government data cited by Bloomberg.Musk’s broadside marks a sharp turn from last year, when SpaceX signed deals with Bharti Airtel and Reliance’s Jio Platforms Ltd. to offer Starlink’s services in India.Bharti is one of the largest shareholders in Eutelsat Communications, operator of the Eutelsat OneWeb satellite network that’s one of Starlink’s biggest low-Earth orbit competitors worldwide.Reliance has its own satellite ambitions through Jio Satellite Communications and its joint venture with Luxembourg-based satellite operator SES SA.Jio, OneWeb and Starlink are among the three companies that have received India’s satellite-communications licenses, although none has yet fully switched on commercial services, Bloomberg reported.In June, it was reported that India had effectively frozen final approvals for Starlink’s commercial launch due to security concerns. Security agencies under the country’s home ministry withheld clearances for the low-Earth orbit service to begin operations, sources had told Bloomberg.Starlink has secured a satellite communications license in India, but is still waiting for the security clearances as well as the spectrum before it can switch on commercially.

item.title: Venezuela's Nicolas Maduro, wife to face new charges in US: ‘Detained Americans were tortured’ — What we know so far
item.description: The US reportedly accused ousted Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro's government of detaining Americans as leverage to extract concessions such as relief from financial sanctions.
item.dc:creator: Akriti Anand
item.content:encoded: Ousted Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores may face new criminal charges in the United States over allegations that Americans detained in Venezuela were tortured, a US official said on Wednesday. The official told Reuters that the new charges could come as soon as Thursday.What do we know about new charges against Maduro, wife? The possibility of new charges was first reported by CNN on Wednesday. Details of the new charges, including the identities of the alleged torture victims, were not immediately available. The US reportedly accused Maduro's government of detaining Americans as leverage to extract concessions such as relief from financial sanctions. Americans whom the US classified as wrongfully detained during Maduro's tenure included five oil executives arrested on graft charges. They were freed in 2022 in exchange for two of Flores' nephews who had been convicted in the US of drug trafficking.Others detained included two former US Army Special Forces members who were arrested in Venezuela in 2020 in connection with a botched raid aimed at ousting Maduro. They were freed in 2023 as part of another prisoner swap, Reuters reported.A spokesperson for the Manhattan US Attorney's office, which brought the charges, declined to comment. Lawyers for Maduro and Flores did not immediately respond to requests for comment.Maduro's captureMaduro, 63, and Flores, 69, were captured by the US military from their home in Caracas on January 3 and brought to New York to face drug trafficking charges. They have been held in a federal jail in Brooklyn.They have pleaded not guilty and are scheduled to go on trial starting June 1, 2027.Flores is due to appear in Manhattan federal court on Thursday to urge US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein to release her from jail before trial for health reasons. Prosecutors oppose her release.Since Maduro's capture, Venezuela has been led by his former vice president, Delcy Rodriguez, who has increased cooperation with the Trump administration.
